title: Poor Pigs
summary: Determine the minimum number of pigs required to identify the single poisonous bucket among a set of buckets, within a specified time limit, by feeding the pigs various combinations of buckets and observing their survival outcomes.
statement: Determine the minimum number of pigs required to identify the single poisonous bucket among a set of buckets, within a specified time limit, by feeding the pigs various combinations of buckets and observing their survival outcomes.
constraints: 1 <= buckets <= 1000; time values are positive and minutes_to_test >= minutes_to_die.
All pigs may participate in every testing round until they die.
reference_solution:
def minimum_test_pigs(buckets, minutes_to_die, minutes_to_test):
 rounds=minutes_to_test//minutes_to_die;states=rounds+1;pigs=0;capacity=1
 while capacity<buckets:pigs+=1;capacity*=states
 return pigs

def minimum_test_pigs(buckets, minutes_to_die, minutes_to_test):
 states=minutes_to_test//minutes_to_die
 if states<=1:return buckets-1
 pigs=0;capacity=1
 while capacity<buckets:pigs+=1;capacity*=states
 return pigs
hints: After r rounds, one pig has r+1 distinguishable outcomes: death in each round or survival.
With p pigs, outcome vectors distinguish (r+1)^p buckets.
Increase p until that capacity reaches buckets.
Assigning each bucket a base-(r+1) outcome vector attains the bound, so the first sufficient p is minimal.
editorial: Assigning each bucket a base-(r+1) outcome vector attains the bound, so the first sufficient p is minimal.

tests.explanation: One round gives each pig two outcomes; two pigs distinguish four buckets.
Four rounds give five states per pig, so five pigs distinguish at least 1000 buckets.
